blocks.h2: Who developed, funded, owned and operated the systems?
paras: IBM, VMware, Linux/KVM community, cloud providers, enterprise IT teams, telecom equipment vendors and open-source foundations. These participants had different roles: research sponsorship, equipment supply, network operation, regulation, standardization and service consumption should not be conflated.
Physical servers host guest OS instances; overlays provide logical network segmentation; cloud control planes provision resources through APIs.
Capital equipment and licenses expanded into usage-based cloud, managed services, SaaS subscriptions and platform fees.
Virtualization abstracts resources but does not remove physical dependencies. Business-process digitization is organizational change, not the same technical mechanism as a hypervisor.

A retailer runs its ERP in VMs on shared hosts, uses a virtual network for segmentation, deploys web services in containers and purchases SaaS for HR. These are different abstractions serving different purposes.
The cost center moves from only procuring hardware toward contracts, capacity planning, identity management, usage governance and resilience engineering.
